prose_updates.tldr: In a new calibrated low-rank multi-environment submodel, any finite projected cumulant breakout identifies the structural effect at the population level, even above the inference order cap; within the bounded legal-swap domain, global no-breakout is exactly source-label ambiguous.  A three-environment construction is ambiguous in every pair yet identified jointly.  On bounded first-breakout shells, cumulant-SVD estimation and conservative Anderson--Rubin length have the sharp weak-flag rates, while externally randomized multiplier inversion gives asymptotically exact unconditional coverage throughout the bounded ambient class, including singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance.

project_justification.gap: Kivva et al. establish a simultaneous-source obstruction in a two-environment setting.  That obstruction transfers here only on the explicitly demonstrated pairwise intersection; their published result does not supply positive identification for arbitrary simultaneous shifts, nor the calibrated low-rank multi-environment population frontier proved here.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies a new population class in which latent cumulant-shift profiles occupy an unknown rank-\(d\) plane calibrated by observed treatment contrasts.  A complementary treatment-noise direction can be invisible in every pairwise analysis but visible jointly, separating population identification from bounded inference and legal source swapping.
project_justification.fill: The results give an explicit unrestricted-order population identifying quotient, an exact if-and-only-if frontier on the bounded legal-swap domain, a legal three-environment pairwise-ambiguous joint-rescue witness, the sharp \(d+2\) environment and delayed-order constructions, shell-specific estimation and conservative-length rates, an ambient-class generated-projector expansion, and externally randomized singularity-safe calibration.  Estimator and conservative-length upper bounds hold over every fixed admissible bounded class, whereas matching minimax lower bounds are certified only on one fixed compatible experiment.

prose_updates.related_work: Kivva, Akbari, Salehkaleybar, and Kiyavash (2025), especially Theorem 3.6 and its source-swap argument, provide the closest two-environment obstruction.  Their positive-radius local analytic-moment condition implies finite absolute moments of every order, but their theorem is invoked only for the demonstrated pairwise intersection; this paper's low-rank calibrated population class is new and does not claim positive identification for arbitrary simultaneous shifts in their class.  Rothenhäusler, Heinze, Peters, and Meinshausen (2015) study BACKSHIFT's different covariance joint-diagonalization geometry.  Higher-cumulant work by Cai et al. (2023), Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025), and Tramontano et al. (2025) uses one-latent-component, targeted-intervention, proxy, or instrumental structure rather than the source-label frontier here.  Long et al. (2023) provide an environmental GMM template, while Andrews and Guggenberger (2019) study singularity-robust testing for supplied moments; neither supplies the same-sample cumulant-plane correction or the structural weak-flag lower-bound family.  Sachs et al. (2005) supply the multi-perturbation protein-signaling setting, and Mooij, Magliacane, and Claassen (2020) explain its latent-confounding and intervention-target complications; neither source verifies the new profile restriction empirically.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded inference results are fixed-dimensional and use balanced deterministic environment shares, a fixed calibration singular gap, and a \(2R_{\max}+\delta\) source-moment envelope.  Estimator risk and conservative expected-length upper bounds are uniform over each fixed admissible bounded class, but the matching full-observation minimax lower bounds are proved only on one fixed compatible experiment, not on every arbitrary nonempty shell.  The randomized multiplier interval has asymptotically exact unconditional coverage over the ambient bounded class under external Gaussian and Monte Carlo randomization, including singular, rank-changing, and zero influence covariance; no finite-sample exactness, conditional-on-randomization validity, expected-length optimality, or diameter optimality is claimed for \(\mathcal C_n^{\mathrm{RJ}}\).
prose_updates.honest_scope: The broad positive result is conditional on the newly imposed calibrated low-rank population class \(\Theta_{\mathrm{pop}}\); it is not a theorem for arbitrary simultaneous latent- and treatment-noise shifts.  The global if-and-only-if statement remains confined to the bounded union \(\mathcal D_\rho\), whose no-breakout branch requires an explicitly legal interior source-swapped partner.  Global real-MGF finiteness is not used and is replaced in the bounded class by finite absolute moments of every integer order; Kivva et al.'s local analytic condition is mentioned only because it implies that weaker moment requirement.  A finite scan through \(R_{\max}\) does not certify global no-breakout, although any later population breakout still identifies.  Conservative \(\mathcal C_n\) coverage holds on the bounded ambient class, but its risk and expected-length rate statements are shell-specific.  Matching minimax lower bounds hold only on one fixed compatible experiment.  The Sachs application is a consumer illustration, not evidence that calibration rank, the latent profile plane, or the singular gap holds in those data.
